# Corns and calluses

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Pediatric dermatology > Corns and calluses*

[Original Article Link](/library/bG0HBh)

---

## Summary

<u>Corns</u> and calluses are thickened areas of <u>skin</u> due to repeated pressure, friction, or irritation. <u>Corns</u> are well-defined horny <u>papules</u> or <u>nodules</u> that are often painful when pressed. Calluses are poorly defined areas of thickened <u>skin</u> that may be painful if <u>cracks</u> develop. Treatment is typically conservative, consisting of soaks, gentle exfoliation, moisturizing creams, topical <u>keratolytic agents</u>, and padding. Large and/or painful lesions may require scalpel <u>debridement</u> or surgical removal. The underlying mechanical cause (e.g., poorly fitted shoes, underlying foot and <u>toe deformities</u>) must also be addressed to prevent recurrence.
